answer: The tide multiplier is published, charged in marble, and velvet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4924 identities would post 637 proofs and burn roughly 13 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
